items.title: In second letter to KP police chief, assembly speaker Swati seeks details of 'detained' lawmakers, ministers
items.description:
PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati has sought details from police of provincial cabinet members and lawmakers who have been “detained or arrested”, it emerged on Sunday.

items.title: Bill Gates joins calls for AI safeguards, including legislation
items.description:
Artificial intelligence requires safeguards that go beyond self-regulation, Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates said in an interview that aired on Sunday, calling for legislation to be passed in Congress.
“You need law enforcement and the politicians to get into the discussion about what safeguards and monitoring look like,” Gates said in a taped interview on NBC’s “Meet the Press” programme. “And that has to be a required thing.”

items.title: Number of unfrozen lakes in Pakistan grows by 65 in less than 2 months: Suparco
items.description:
ISLAMABAD: The number of unfrozen lakes in Pakistan grew from 40 to 105 in less than two months, according to satellite imagery assessed by the national space agency of Pakistan between July and August.
Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (Suparco) said in a press release that the latest assessment was based on temporal satellite imagery, with the the latest image acquired on Aug 5. All identified lakes were mapped on optical satellite imagery to estimate their surface area and to determine whether they were frozen or unfrozen, it noted.

items.description:

items.description:
Adviser to the Finance Minister Khurram Schehzad clarified on Sunday that the government was not buying any aircraft for Pakistan International Airlines (PIA), which was privatised through an auction in December last year.
“The government is neither buying aircraft for a privatised PIA, nor has it announced any sovereign guarantee of taxpayer-funded loan for doing so,” Schehzad posted on X following claims on social media that a minister was arranging and negotiating sovereign-linked financing for the jets.

items.title: War in the Gulf
items.description:
THE war that the US and Israel imposed on Iran this year has failed to achieve any of the objectives that the two countries had intended. The declared purpose was to prevent Iran from building a nuclear weapon.
A fact-check indicates that Iran had kept its civil nuclear programme under IAEA safeguards. It had also willingly agreed to a nuclear deal in 2015. items.title: Swiss vote on what it means to be neutral
items.description:
The Swiss voted on Sunday on a much-debated proposal to tighten their country’s cherished neutrality, with polls indicating most would reject the initiative championed by the hard-right and dubbed “pro-Russian” by opponents.
Polling stations opened on Sunday morning for in-person voting on those and other topics as part of Switzerland’s direct democracy system, although most people vote in advance by post.
The Swiss widely embrace their neutrality, but an initiative to enshrine a strict definition into the constitution has exposed deep disagreement over what that neutrality entails.

items.title: Gunmen kill 27 in 2 separate shootings in South Africa
items.description:
Gunmen killed at least 27 people in two mass shootings in South Africa’s two main cities, police said on Sunday, in the latest violence to hit the crime-weary country.
Eight gunmen armed with assault rifles stormed a bar west of Johannesburg at around 1930 GMT (12:30am) on Saturday, killing 17 people and wounding 15 others.
The victims included 13 males and four females.
The suspects opened fire on customers drinking outside and then moved inside to continue shooting, police said.

items.title: Newly inducted Hangor-class submarine conducts maiden live weapon firing in Arabian Sea: ISPR
items.description:
The navy’s first Hangor-class submarine successfully conducted its maiden live weapon firing in the Arabian Sea, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Sunday.
The Hangor-class submarine arrived at Karachi Port in June, underscoring the deepening strategic defence cooperation between Pakistan and China.
Terming it a “major demonstration of operational readiness”, ISPR said the newly inducted PNS/M HANGOR accurately engaged a “designated long-range target with an anti-ship cruise missile” during the weapon firing exercise.

items.title: Hamas leader says Israel to campaign off Gaza's 'blood' in election
items.description:
The leader of Hamas brushed aside the possibility of change from Israel’s upcoming election in an interview on Saturday, saying he expected Israelis to campaign off Gaza’s “blood”.
“Whether this or that person comes to power, or this party or another —  our people have suffered at the hands of all Israeli parties,”  Khalil al-Hayya told the Qatari station Al-Araby.
“We absolutely refuse to allow the blood, suffering, and cause of the Palestinian people to serve as fuel for Israeli elections. What matters to us is that our people achieve their goals, aspirations and legitimate rights.”

items.description:
LAHORE: Four patients undergoing dialysis at the Tehsil Headquarters Hospital (THQ), Mian Channu, have tested positive for HIV, raising fresh concerns about infection-control practices at healthcare facilities in south Punjab.
According to the reports available with Dawn, the patients, including three women, who had been receiving dialysis at the hospital tested positive for the deadly virus after initial diagnosis.

items.title: Polling concludes in Bahawalpur's NA-168 by-election
items.description:
BAHAWALPUR: The voting process concluded peacefully on Sunday in the by-poll for Bahawalpur’s NA-168 constituency.
While official results were not released until midnight, reports suggested that PML-N’s Malik Munir Iqbal, brother of Punjab Assembly Deputy Speaker Malik Zaheer Iqbal Channar, was leading the race.
The seat fell vacant after the death of Munir’s father, Malik Muhammad Iqbal Channar in August.
